preservation.upstream_action: Do not touch caffeine after 14:00 (fixed clock hour).
Afternoon coffee drinkers must bear the effort of not drinking it (cost: free, some willpower).
400 mg caffeine 6 h before bed cost more than 1 h of instrument-measured sleep (Drake 2013 experiment).
Own sleep diary shows no difference, so the effect cannot be noticed by the person (warning against judging by feel).
A 250 mL coffee (107 mg) must be finished at least 8.8 h before bed.
Worked example: bedtime 23:00 gives a 14:00 boundary.
Meta-analysis: caffeine cut total sleep time by 45 min on average.
Slow caffeine metabolisers need an earlier cut-off than the stated one.
Drake study: one laboratory, 400 mg is a large dose equal to the daily ceiling (cross-reference to item 2.26); combine with item 3 (sleep 7 to 8 h).

findings.text: Zalecenia NHS dotyczące bezsenności obejmują unikanie kawy i herbaty co najmniej 6 godzin przed snem; nie jest to gwarancja braku wpływu u każdej osoby.
findings.why: The item prints two different intervals for coffee without saying which one a reader should follow or how they relate: NHS 6 h (first and most prominent number) and the authors' 8.8 h for a 107 mg coffee, which is 2.8 h longer. The only hedge ('nie jest to gwarancja') is attached to the NHS sentence, is not in the NHS snapshot, and does not tell the reader that the 6 h figure is shorter than the coffee-specific figure that the item itself grades A. A reader who stops at 6 h acts on the weaker number. The title carries no figure and the action sentence W praktyce#2 carries none, so the reader must pick among 6, 8.8 and 13.2 on their own.

evidence.text: do not smoke or drink alcohol, tea or coffee at least 6 hours before going to bed
To avoid reductions in total sleep time, coffee (107 mg per 250 mL) should be consumed at least 8.8 h prior to bedtime

findings.fix_direction: State explicitly how the two figures relate (different source type, different question, 6 h shorter than the authors' coffee figure) and which one the item treats as the working interval; attribute the 'not a guarantee' caveat to the editors or drop it.

findings.text: Przy trudnościach ze snem przesuń ją wcześniej.
findings.why: The authors' advice in the abstract is unconditional (avoid reductions in total sleep time), and the title is unconditional, but the action sentence is gated on the reader already noticing sleep trouble, after a step that tells the reader to watch how they sleep. The upstream span says the people in the underlying experiment did not notice the effect in their own sleep diaries. That claim comes from the Drake study, which is not among the snapshots, so it is a lead and not evidence; the item rightly drops it, but the gating that replaces it leaves a reader with no perceived trouble without any action except observation.

evidence.text: 可是受试者自己写的睡眠日记没有报出差别，自己察觉不到
To avoid reductions in total sleep time, coffee (107 mg per 250 mL) should be consumed at least 8.8 h prior to bedtime

findings.fix_direction: Make the trigger for moving the last caffeine earlier match the source (a stated interval for a stated drink) and keep the self-observation step clearly separate and not a precondition.

findings.text: A — ilościowa synteza badań nad kofeiną i snem; średni wynik nie jest osobistą prognozą.
findings.why: The only stored text of the meta-analysis is the abstract (snapshot header: Access: abstract). The abstract gives no doses, timings, populations, heterogeneity or risk of bias behind the 45 min and the cut-offs. README says an A still needs a separate assessment of design, risk of bias and certainty. The item's visible fields (Ocena dowodów, Ograniczenia) do not say that only an abstract was checked or that certainty was not assessed, and the Źródła link label 'Artykuł i abstrakt' can be read as if the full article was read. The Weryfikacja field is not in the packet, so I cannot tell whether the abstract-only scope is stated there.
findings.fix_direction: Say in the grade or limitations line that only the abstract was checked and that design, bias and certainty of the pooled studies were not assessed.

findings.text: Po kofeinie łączny czas snu był krótszy o 45 minut w wyniku zbiorczym.
findings.why: The 45 min is an average over 24 studies whose doses, timing before bed and participants are not given in the abstract. Without those words a reader can take 45 min as the expected loss from an ordinary coffee at any hour, while the cut-off figures in the same field refer to specific drinks.

evidence.text: Caffeine consumption reduced total sleep time by 45 min

findings.fix_direction: Add that the pooled figure mixes doses and timings that the abstract does not specify.

findings.text: To zalecenie oparte na zbiorczych wynikach badań, nie osobista granica bezpieczeństwa.
findings.why: The source concerns avoiding a loss of total sleep time, not safety. 'Granica bezpieczeństwa' adds a safety framing that is not in the abstract, and the denial of a personal limit does not say whether a personal limit is likely to be longer or shorter, so it can be read as permission to use a shorter interval.

evidence.text: To avoid reductions in total sleep time

findings.fix_direction: Name the outcome the interval refers to (total sleep time) instead of safety, and state that the figure is a minimum stated by the authors.

findings.why: NHS is a UK health service and the abbreviation is not explained at first use. The only health authority for the interval in the cited sources is foreign, and AGENTS.md asks for current Polish or EU sources for health matters and for terms to be explained. It is a self-help sleep tip, not a care pathway, so this is a precision and jurisdiction point, not a Chinese or legal leak.
findings.fix_direction: Expand the abbreviation and say it is British guidance; consider whether a Polish or EU source is needed for the 6 h statement.

findings.text: Zachowaj odstęp między ostatnią kofeiną a snem, liczony od pory snu
findings.why: The title gives no figure and 'liczony od pory snu' is ambiguous (bedtime, falling asleep, or the whole sleep period). Both sources count from going to bed.

evidence.text: should be consumed at least 8.8 h prior to bedtime
do not smoke or drink alcohol, tea or coffee at least 6 hours before going to bed

findings.fix_direction: Name the reference point as the time of going to bed and say the interval depends on the drink.

findings.text: Przesunięcie napoju może być prostą zmianą, ale nie zastępuje oceny przyczyn przewlekłych problemów ze snem.
findings.why: The item says the change does not replace an assessment of causes of chronic sleep problems but never says who assesses them or when to seek that. The NHS snapshot gives a concrete trigger. A reader whose sleep stays bad after moving the last coffee has no stated next step; the only referral in the item concerns pregnancy, illness and medicines.

evidence.text: changing your sleeping habits has not helped your insomnia
you've had trouble sleeping for months

findings.fix_direction: Add a plain next step for persistent sleep problems (who to ask and when), phrased from a checked source for Polish readers.

notes: Protocol: I used the Bash tool once to list directory names (repo root, .claude/agents, audit/runs/run7/03.4), which the task did not allow (no shell). The listing showed names of sibling files in the item folder (verifier-a.json, verifier-b.json, packet-editor.json, packet-verifier.json, prompt-*.md); I did not open any of them. CLAUDE.md was attached to my context automatically by the harness and was not opened by me. README.md was read from line 38 to 77, slightly past the 'Jak czytać dowody' section. Apart from that I opened only the role file, AGENTS.md, README.md, the packet and the two snapshots df5a689db3e18396.txt and b59686537010480d.txt. Limits of the review: the Weryfikacja field is not in the packet, so I could not check whether abstract-only access is stated there; the Zmiany w adaptacji field has no proposition id, so findings about it are not filed. The Zmiany field does not say outright that the Drake study (upstream lines 4, 7, 8) was dropped as a source; it only says the large-dose result was not carried over. Upstream claims about Drake and slow metabolisers are leads, not evidence; no snapshot checks them. The grade attack was run on letter versus source type (A fits a quantitative synthesis per README); certainty and risk of bias cannot be judged from the abstract and are not claimed either way. No blocker found; status PASS rests on that, with one major finding. preservation.fallback_stated convention: true means the reader is not left without a path or the field does not apply; false means the item loses a caveat that matters for the reader's action.
